news.drawAway: The balls have been drawn. You travel to {opp} for the {comp} {stg_k}. {tail_k}
news.drawTailAway: Quiet the crowd early and anything is possible.
news.finalsWeekend: {venue} stages both European finals this season: the Continental Shield under Friday lights, the Continental Cup on the Saturday. {seats} seats in {city}, the whole sport in town. Eight quarter-finalists stand in each, and all circled the date this morning.
news.natFilled: Kick-off was coming and the squad was short, so your assistant added {n} to make up the numbers. They are named on merit, not on your judgement - next window, name it yourself.
news.natName: The camp is open and the sheet is blank. {nationCap_k} need a squad named before the first Test - at least {n} of them - and the country desk has everyone available, with the coaches' picks at the top. This one is yours: nobody is going to name it for you.
news.lionsCallA:
The call every player in these islands dreams of: {names} {is_k} going on {tour}. The whole club walks taller this morning.
{he_k} will be away for the tour window. Plan the run-in accordingly - and welcome back a Lion.
news.lionsCallB:
The {tour} squad is out, and the club's name is on it: {names}. Training stopped for the announcement. Nobody minded.
{he_k} will be away for the tour window. Plan the run-in accordingly - and welcome back a Lion.
news.callUps: The following players have been called up and will be unavailable during the international window: {names}.
news.lionsHome: Back in club colours after {tour}: {names}. Win or lose, a tour changes a player - {come_k} back a bigger presence in this dressing room. The medical staff still counsel care: a Lions summer empties the tank like nothing else.
news.lionsHomeWonSubj: 🦁 The Lions come home as series winners
news.lionsHomeWon: Back in club colours after {tour}: {names}. A series win in the luggage, and the kind of standing money cannot buy. Expect {him_k} to walk taller here too. The medical staff still counsel care: a Lions summer empties the tank like nothing else.
news.intlBack: Back in club colours: {names}. The medical staff's advice is blunt: Test rugby empties the tank, and none of them are at full freshness this week. Rotate or risk it - your call.
news.mentorLost: With {mentor} gone, {kid} is training alone again. The academy coach will keep an eye on him - but it isn't the same.

wantsTerms.one: {player}'s agent has been on the phone: his client is playing the house down (avg {avg}) on {wage}/week, and the market rate is well north of that. He has {n} year left, but leave it unresolved and his head will drop - and other clubs will smell it. Offer a new deal from his player page.
wantsTerms.other: {player}'s agent has been on the phone: his client is playing the house down (avg {avg}) on {wage}/week, and the market rate is well north of that. He has {n} years left, but leave it unresolved and his head will drop - and other clubs will smell it. Offer a new deal from his player page.

news.agentPublic: Two months of silence from the club, so the agent has taken it to the papers: "{player} is one of the best-performing players in the league and the club knows our position." Rival clubs will have noticed. Sort a new deal on his player page - or brace for bids.
news.becomesMentor: The coaches have noticed it in the little things - the extras after training, the way he talks in the huddle. {player} is starting to carry himself like {mentor}. Character: now {pers_k}.
news.aheadOfSchedule: Good news from the treatment table: {player} ({injury_k}) has smashed his rehab targets and is available again this week - earlier than anyone dared hope.
news.backInTraining: Available for selection again: {men_l}. Pick a rusty man now and he could break down again; ease him back and he will be right.
news.wPeaceBrokered: The manager got them in a room and shut the door. Both men came out and trained. Nobody is pretending they are friends, but the squad can get on with its week.
news.wTalksFail: The manager tried to settle it between {a} and {b} and got nowhere. Worse, the squad knows the meeting happened - and that it did not work.
news.wPeace1: Clear-the-air talks at the training ground this week. {a} and {b} trained together on Thursday and the squad say the atmosphere has lifted. One senior player: "It's done. We move."
news.wPeace2: Whatever was said between {a} and {b}, it worked: the pair ran the same drills all week and shared a bench at lunch. The squad has quietly exhaled.
news.wPeace3: {a} and {b} shook hands in front of the group on Monday, which is how these things end in rugby: no statement, no ceremony, back to work.
news.wFrosty1: Sources close to the squad say {a} and {b} are still not speaking. Team-mates are starting to pick sides - the sort of thing that costs points.
news.wFrosty2: {a} and {b} warmed up at opposite ends of the pitch again this week. The coaches pretend not to notice. The players notice everything.
news.wFrosty3: No thaw yet between {a} and {b}: separate gym slots, separate tables, one very tired captain shuttling between them.
news.wRift: The Wire understands {a} ({aPers_k}) and {b} ({bPers_k}) had {flash_k}. Coaches separated the pair. Expect the mood to suffer until it's resolved - keep winning and these things heal quicker.
news.wCommunity1: The whole squad spent Wednesday coaching at local schools and visiting the children's ward. Corny? Maybe. But the group came back closer, and the town noticed.
news.wCommunity2: School visits, hospital wards, a hundred wonky selfies: the squad gave the town its Wednesday. The bus home was loud in the good way.
news.wBoot1: {player} has signed a personal sponsorship with a boot manufacturer. His locker now contains fourteen boxes of boots and one very smug grin.
news.wBoot2: A boot brand has put {player} on a personal deal. The first shipment arrived in club colours; the second, mysteriously, in gold. The forwards have thoughts.
news.wGround1: The head groundsman has banned the forwards from 'his' pitch until Thursday after last week's scrummaging session left it looking ploughed. The pack are training on the back field, muttering.
news.wGround2: An uneasy truce at {stadium}: the groundsman has chalked a line beyond which "no scrummaging shall occur". The pack are testing its legal force one metre at a time.
news.wAdvert1: {player} spent his day off filming a regional car dealership advert. Team-mates have already obtained the script. Training may include dramatic readings.
news.wAdvert2: {player} is the new face of a local bathroom showroom. The billboard goes up next month. The dressing room has already ordered a framed print for his locker.
news.wChef1: The performance department has brought in {chef_k} for the rest of the season. The senior pros are sceptical. The young lads are all-in. Someone has already broken the new equipment.
news.wChef2: {short} have added {chef_k} to the backroom staff. Week one verdict from the front row: "interesting". Week one verdict from the academy: total religious conversion.
news.wBug1: The medical room is standing-room only: {names} have all been laid low by a virus doing the rounds. They'll play if picked, but the tanks won't be full this week. The kit man is bleaching everything.
news.wBug2: {names} all called in pale and shivering this week. The doctor's diagnosis: "the thing that's going round." They can play, but do not expect eighty full-blooded minutes.
news.wBug3: A virus has worked through the squad faster than any defensive drill: {names} are all below par. Training moved outdoors, soup was served, and the physio room smells of eucalyptus.
news.wTakeoverHardens: The consortium linked with {club} has reportedly entered exclusivity. Due diligence is under way; the current owners are said to be "open to the right offer". Supporters dare to dream of a war chest.
news.wTakeoverOff: After weeks of whispers, the money men have walked away from {club} - "valuation gap", say sources. The club statement thanks supporters for their patience and says it remains "well capitalised". Nobody is convinced.
news.wTakeoverCircle: A wealthy consortium - the names change depending on who you ask - has been linked with a takeover of {club}. A private jet at the local airfield has done a lot of heavy lifting in the fan forums. Most of these stories die quietly; some don't.
news.wRumour1: {buyerName} have sent scouts to {ownerPoss} last three matches - the man they're watching is {player}.
news.wRumour2: Agents claim {buyer} are readying a {fee} bid for {player}. {owner} insist he is going nowhere.
news.wRumour3: {player} to {buyer}? A source at the player's management agency says "there is interest, and it's serious."
news.wRumour4: Whispers from {buyerCity}: {buyerPoss} head coach has made {player} his number one target.
news.wAgent1: {player} is out of contract at the end of the season and his agent is doing the media rounds: "My client loves the club, but he wants to feel loved back. We are listening to what's out there." Sort a new deal - or cash in.
news.wAgent2: Six months left on {player}'s deal and his agent has started answering the phone on the first ring. "No comment" has never carried so much comment. Renew him or price him.
news.wAgent3: The contract clock is ticking on {player}, and this week his agent was photographed at lunch with two directors of rugby who were not yours. Draw your own conclusions - everyone else has.
news.grForumExitSubj: FAN FORUM: "{starLast} to leave?" thread hits 400 replies in a night
news.grForumExit: One unsourced post claiming {star} has "told friends he wants out" has produced four hundred replies, two spin-off threads and a poll. There is no agent, no journalist and no evidence. Page nine is arguing about the stadium car park. One moderator: "Every year. Same thread. Same fella posting it."
news.grSocialClipSubj: SOCIAL: eleven seconds of {star} in training breaks containment
news.grSocialClip: Two million views and counting for a clip of {star} doing something that should not be physically available to a man that size. The comments are split between awe and accusations of a smaller pitch. {shortPoss} media team have posted it, deleted it, and posted it again with worse music.
news.grPodcastKebabSubj: PODCAST: {star}'s cheat meal confession divides the nation
news.grPodcastKebab: Forty minutes of genuinely excellent lineout detail earned nothing. One sentence about a Friday kebab has produced eight hundred quote tweets and a statement from a rival takeaway offering him a sponsorship. The {short} nutritionist has requested a right of reply and has been told the slot is full.
news.grAiGraphicSubj: BROADCAST: graphics package gives {starLast} six fingers and a new name
news.grAiGraphic: The pre-match player card rendered {star} with an extra finger, a surname spelled two different ways in the same graphic, and a career-tries figure that would make him the leading scorer in the sport's history. The broadcaster has apologised. The screenshot is already a profile picture.
news.grStatAccountSubj: STATS ACCOUNT: {short} are top of a table nobody asked for
news.grStatAccount: A popular numbers account has crunched carries into contact per phase in the opposition 22 on grounds above sea level and declared {short} the best team in the league. Fans of {short} have adopted the metric as gospel. Everyone else has pointed out that it also ranks a pub side above the world champions.
news.grPunditGemSubj: PUNDIT COLUMN: "{short} have unearthed a gem"
news.grPunditGem: This week's big read calls {kid}, {kidAge}, "the most natural {kidPos} of his generation" and notes that half the league already knows. {short} supporters have spent the day politely asking the columnist to be quiet, delete it, and consider a career in something else. The columnist has replied to eleven of them individually. He is enjoying this enormously.
news.grSchoolVisitSubj: WHOLESOME: {kid} shows up to a school assembly and stays two hours
news.grSchoolVisit: A local primary asked the {short} academy whether anyone could hand out a reading prize. {kid} arrived early, stayed two hours and signed everything put in front of him including the lectern and one teacher's laptop lid. The video has more views than the club's last three tries combined.
news.grAgentFlatteredSubj: AGENT TALK: {target} "flattered" by the interest, says everyone
news.grAgentFlattered: {target}'s representatives declined every opportunity to hose this down: "My client is very happy at {other}. But every player listens." Rugby's translation service has been working overtime. The fan forums did the rest before lunch.
news.grForumDreamSubj: FAN FORUM: the "realistic transfer targets" thread is anything but
news.grForumDream: The {short} thread is titled "realistic targets" and {target} appears on every page of it. The finances are impossible, the positional fit is questionable and the enthusiasm is absolute. Somebody has made a graphic. Somebody else has made a better one.
news.grRefMicSubj: REF MIC: the clip every group chat is quoting
news.grRefMic: A referee's exchange with a front row from the weekend has escaped containment: "You are not bound. You have never been bound." Refereeing socials are calling it a masterclass in communication. Props are calling it slander and have opened a group chat of their own.
news.grPropGymSubj: SOCIAL: {propLast} lifts something he should not have lifted
news.grPropGym: {prop} has posted a gym clip that the strength coach describes, on the record, as "not a programmed movement". It has a hundred thousand views and a duet from a professional strongman who appears genuinely concerned. The {short} physio has commented on it too. His comment is one full stop.
news.grPropMarathonSubj: CHARITY: {propLast} agrees to a half marathon before reading the word half
news.grPropMarathon: A supporters' club raffle has committed {prop} to thirteen miles for charity. He accepted on camera, confidently, then asked a follow-up question that revealed he had heard "half an hour". The fundraising total has tripled since the clip went up.
news.grNineMicSubj: REF MIC: {nineLast} spends eighty minutes coaching the referee
news.grNineMic: The audio from the weekend has {nine} offering the official guidance on the offside line, the tackle height, the clock and, at one point, the official's own positioning. The referee's reply has been turned into a ringtone. Nobody involved regrets anything.
news.grKitLeakSubj: SOCIAL: {shortPoss} new shirt leaks a day early, on a bad mannequin
news.grKitLeak: Next season's kit appeared on a reseller feed before the launch, photographed on a mannequin with one arm and a haunted expression. The club is furious. The fans have moved past the club's feelings and are now conducting a full referendum on the collar. Verdict: divisive.
news.grGroundsmanSubj: GROUNDSMAN WATCH: visiting coach calls the {stadium} pitch "a ploughed field"
news.grGroundsman: The head groundsman has responded through visibly gritted teeth that "the surface rewards a team willing to keep the ball in hand". The visiting coach has kept a boot as evidence and photographed it next to a ruler. The groundsman has photographed the ruler.
news.grMascotSubj: MASCOT INCIDENT: the {short} mascot is trending for all the wrong reasons
news.grMascot: A half-time penalty shootout ended with the mascot taking out a nine-year-old at the knees and celebrating in front of the family stand. The club has issued an apology. The mascot has issued nothing, because the mascot is committed to the bit, and gained forty thousand followers overnight.
news.grAnnouncerSubj: STADIUM PA: announcer reads out the wrong team, then doubles down
news.grAnnouncer: The {stadium} announcer named the entire opposition XV as the home side, realised at fifteen, and elected to finish the list anyway "for consistency". The crowd applauded every name. Away supporters have started a petition to have him do their team sheet every week.
news.grPieSubj: CATERING: the {short} pie has been reviewed, and the review is 900 words
news.grPie: A widely followed food account has awarded the ground's steak pie a mark of 6.4 with the note "structurally ambitious, emotionally cold". The club has responded by putting the score on a chalkboard outside the kiosk. Sales are up thirty per cent. The pie has not changed.
news.grDroneSubj: TRAINING LEAK: a drone over {short} training gets exactly nothing
news.grDrone: Somebody flew a drone over a closed session hoping for the team sheet and captured forty minutes of a squad doing a passing drill in complete silence, plus one man tying a lace for nine of them. The footage has been posted anyway. It has done numbers.
news.grSeagullSubj: WILDLIFE: a seagull holds up play at {stadium} for two minutes
news.grSeagull: A single gull occupied the 22 and declined every invitation to leave, including one from a second row who tried reasoning. Play resumed when the bird took a pie from row three and departed on its own terms. It now has a fan account with more followers than two of the players.
news.grMerchTypoSubj: MERCH: {short} sell out of a shirt with a spelling mistake on it
news.grMerchTypo: A print run went out with the club motto missing a letter, which the club discovered from a supporter's post rather than from the supplier. The recall lasted ninety minutes before somebody noticed the mistaken ones were reselling for triple. The recall has been quietly cancelled.
news.grBannerSubj: TERRACES: {short} fans unveil a banner nobody can read
news.grBanner: Months of planning went into a full-length tifo for the weekend, and it went up upside down and back to front. From the far stand it appears to say something rude about {short} themselves. The group behind it has declared this "the intended reading all along" and is taking commissions.
news.grStreamSubj: BROADCAST: the {short} stream cuts to a fixed shot of a car park for six minutes
news.grStream: A gallery mix-up sent the live feed to an unmanned camera pointed at the players' entrance during the busiest passage of the match. Nineteen thousand people watched a car park and, by minute four, were commentating on it. The clip has outperformed the highlights.
news.grSponsorSubj: SPONSORS: {shortPoss} new partner is a funeral director and the fans love it
news.grSponsor: The commercial team expected a mild reaction to the sleeve deal and instead got the best day their social accounts have ever had. Supporters were asked for a slogan and thousands answered, most unprintable. The winner goes on the sleeve next week: "With you at the death."
news.grWeatherSubj: WEATHER: hail stops the {short} warm-up and starts a snowball fight
news.grWeather: Sixty seconds of freak hail emptied the pitch and produced footage of two professional squads abandoning their preparation to pelt each other in front of an empty stand. Both head coaches have described it as "not ideal". Both clubs' accounts have posted it.
news.grBusSubj: LOGISTICS: the {short} team bus takes a wrong turn into a wedding
news.grBus: A satnav sent the coach down a lane and into the car park of a hotel mid-reception. The squad were applauded in, photographed with the couple, and applauded out. The bride's cousin has since been photographed at {stadium} in a replica shirt.
news.grQuizSubj: SOCIAL: {short} players fail a quiz about their own club, publicly
news.grQuiz: The media team filmed a light-hearted club history quiz and released it without watching it back. Nobody named the ground's record attendance, one man guessed the club was founded in 1998, and the captain named a competition that has never existed. It is the club's most watched video of the season.
news.grCatSubj: WILDLIFE: a cat is now a member of the {short} coaching staff
news.grCat: A stray that adopted the training ground gates has been photographed sitting in on the forwards' meeting, on the whiteboard side of the room. The club has given it a name, a bowl and, this week, a squad number in the region of 47. The kit man is drafting a shirt.
news.grTmoSubj: TMO: eight minutes to decide something everybody in the ground had decided
news.grTmo: The weekend's showpiece stopped for eight minutes while officials examined a grounding from eleven angles, four of them worse than the naked eye. The eventual decision matched the first replay. Broadcasters have cut it into a montage with a ticking clock and it is doing very well.
news.grKickerNetSubj: SOCIAL: a supporter lands a halfway kick and the internet demands a contract
news.grKickerNet: A half-time competition entrant in jeans and work boots struck one from inside his own half and straight through. He then did it again for the cameras. Two clubs have posted the clip. One head coach has been asked about it in a press conference and did not entirely rule it out.
news.grSheepSubj: VILLAGE RUGBY: match abandoned when forty sheep occupy the home 22
news.grSheep: A gate left open at a sixth-tier fixture admitted an entire flock at a penalty advantage. The referee consulted both captains, consulted the sheep, and abandoned the game with the immortal full-time line: "Gentlemen, they have more numbers and better shape than either defence." The league has ordered a replay. The farmer has ordered a season ticket.
news.grTrophyLostSubj: SILVERWARE: a village club has been polishing the wrong trophy for 41 years
news.grTrophyLost: During an insurance valuation, the county junior cup a village side has displayed since 1984 turned out to be a regional best-kept-allotment award with a rugby ball soldered on. Nobody knows where the real cup went. The club has voted unanimously to keep the allotment one, on the grounds that "we definitely won something, and this is shinier."
news.grPostmanSubj: GRASSROOTS: fourth-tier club discovers their postman has been at every away game for 20 years
news.grPostman: A club historian assembling an anniversary album noticed the same man at the edge of every away photograph since 2006. It is their postman. He has never mentioned it once on his round. Asked why, he said he did not want to make it about him. The club has retired the number 24 in his honour: one for every away shirt he never asked for.
news.grDogTrySubj: VILLAGE RUGBY: a dog scores the decisive try and the league has to rule on it
news.grDogTry: A spaniel invaded a promotion decider, intercepted a flat pass and crossed the line to what witnesses describe as the loudest cheer in the ground's history. The referee disallowed it for offside, reasoning the dog "entered from in front of the kicker". The league has upheld the decision but named the spaniel in its team of the week, at openside.
news.grAnthemSubj: MATCHDAY: the wrong anthem plays and both teams commit to it completely
news.grAnthem: An admin error at a cup tie played the theme from a daytime antiques programme instead of the national anthem. Neither side broke formation. Thirty professional rugby players stood at full attention through ninety seconds of light harpsichord, hands on hearts, and the crowd joined in humming. The clip has more views than the match.
news.grScrumCafeSubj: COMMUNITY: a front row opens a coffee shop where everything is scrum-named and nothing is explained
news.grScrumCafe: Three retired props have opened a cafe with a menu that includes the Loosehead Latte, the Tighthead Flat White and a pastry called the Collapsed Maul, which arrives deliberately flattened. Tourists keep asking why the sugar sachets say "BIND" on them. The owners refuse to say. It is the best-reviewed coffee shop in the county.
news.grLineoutLadderSubj: GRASSROOTS: club banned from using their new lineout tactic involving an actual stepladder
news.grLineoutLadder: An eighth-tier side unveiled a routine in which the hooker threw to a jumper standing on a stepladder painted in club colours. It worked three times before the referee found the relevant law, which took eleven minutes, because nobody had ever needed it before. The league's written ruling begins "with reluctant admiration" and the ladder now hangs in the clubhouse.
news.grFogMatchSubj: WEATHER: two teams play twelve minutes in fog before discovering the ball went home
news.grFogMatch: A cup tie in dense fog continued in fine spirit until both packs converged on a ruck that turned out to be a training bag. Investigation revealed a clearing kick in the third minute had left the ground entirely, and a spectator, believing the game over, had taken the ball home for his son. The league has ordered a replay. The son is keeping the ball.
news.chTale1Subj: CLUBHOUSE: {propLast} wins the squad golf day, refuses to be humble
news.chTale1: {prop} shot the round of his life at the team golf day and has already had the scorecard laminated. It is now blu-tacked inside his locker at eye level. The backs have demanded a recount; the referee (the kit man) says the result stands.
news.chTale2Subj: CLUBHOUSE: ice bath declared too small for the front row
news.chTale2: The new recovery suite opened this week, and within a day the front row lodged a formal complaint that the ice bath "fits one and a half props maximum". A rota has been posted. {prop} has annexed the 6pm slot indefinitely and laminated that too.
news.chTale3Subj: CLUBHOUSE: {lockLast} adopts the groundsman's dog, sort of
news.chTale3: The groundsman's terrier has decided {lock} is its favourite person on earth and now attends every session, sitting neatly beside the tackle bags. The club shop is printing a tiny replica shirt. Nobody has told the groundsman where his dog spends its days, but he probably knows.
news.chTale4Subj: CLUBHOUSE: half-backs in bus playlist standoff
news.chTale4: {nine} and {ten} have shared control of the team bus playlist for two seasons, and the arrangement has finally collapsed over what the squad describe only as "the incident with the sea shanties". A peace deal now alternates song by song. The forwards, who wanted silence, have lost again.
news.chTale5Subj: CLUBHOUSE: {wingLast} loses race to a schoolboy, demands rematch
news.chTale5: At a community visit this week the fastest man at the club was beaten over 40 metres by a twelve-year-old wearing school shoes. {wing} maintains the start was jumped and has formally requested a rematch "on a proper track, with blocks". The twelve-year-old's PE teacher is considering terms.
news.chTale6Subj: CLUBHOUSE: team-room quiz night ends in googling scandal
news.chTale6: Wednesday's quiz night was abandoned at the sports round when one table of forwards answered a question about 1987 with suspicious speed and in full sentences. Phones are now surrendered at the door, and the quizmaster (the physio) has been given "full disciplinary powers". He has had a lanyard made. Nobody knows how to tell him it has gone too far.
news.chTale7Subj: CLUBHOUSE: the kit man's biannual sock audit strikes fear into all
news.chTale7: It is sock audit week. The kit man has counted out, counted back, and found the squad collectively nine pairs short. An amnesty box has appeared outside the changing room with a sign reading "NO QUESTIONS ASKED (THIS TIME)". Three pairs have already been returned under cover of darkness.
news.chTale8Subj: CLUBHOUSE: bus driver gets a guard of honour for his 200th away trip
news.chTale8: Two hundred away trips, zero breakdowns, one legendary flask. The squad formed a guard of honour in the car park this week for the team bus driver, who described it as "completely unnecessary" while visibly delighted. He has been presented with a shirt with WHEELS 1 on the back.
news.lawWatch1Subj: LAW WATCH: 25-point "super try" floated for length-of-the-field scores
news.lawWatch1: A working group has proposed quintuple points for tries begun behind a team's own 22. Coaches call it "bingo rugby". Fans have already built entire imaginary seasons around it. The world governing body stresses it is "one idea among many", which is committee language for never.
news.lawWatch2Subj: LAW WATCH: proposal to reduce teams to 13 players "under review"
news.lawWatch2: A discussion paper suggests trimming the XV to thirteen to "open space and cut collisions". The northern unions are apoplectic, the southern unions intrigued, and one existing sport with exactly that player count is watching with its arms folded. Expect a quiet burial by autumn.
news.lawWatch3Subj: LAW WATCH: shot clock for scrums - 30 seconds or a free-kick
news.lawWatch3: The proposal: packs get half a minute from mark to engagement or concede the put-in. Front rows everywhere describe the idea as "a war crime". Referees privately love it. The trial is earmarked for a development competition nobody can name, which tells you everything.
news.lawWatch4Subj: LAW WATCH: kicks at goal worth less in the final quarter, says think-tank
news.lawWatch4: Penalties would drop to two points after the hour "to encourage ambition". Kickers are furious, flankers delighted, and the fan forums have run the numbers on every classic final and declared history itself invalid. The world governing body thanks the think-tank for its input.
news.lawWatch5Subj: LAW WATCH: unlimited substitutions trial mooted for pre-season
news.lawWatch5: Rolling subs, all match, every match. Conditioning coaches are drooling; purists are drafting strongly worded letters with footnotes. The proposal is "at concept stage", a phrase that has preceded precisely nothing becoming law in the sport's history.
news.lawWatch6Subj: LAW WATCH: golden point extra time for all league matches "on the table"
news.lawWatch6: No more draws, ever, says the paper - first score after 80 wins it. The romantics mourn the honourable draw; the broadcasters have already cut a trailer. The league's fixture staff, asked to model the overtime, sent back a single spreadsheet cell reading "no".
news.wWin1: Three wins on the spin and the {stadium} bars are humming. A supporters' podcast this week: "Whisper it, but this {manager} side might actually be building something."
news.wWin2: Three straight wins and the queue at the club shop has opinions about silverware. The older heads keep saying "long season" and grinning while they say it.
news.wWin3: The terraces have a new song and it has {manager} in it. Three wins running will do that. Keep winning and they will add verses.
news.wWin4: Three on the bounce, and the man who runs the burger van says takings are up - "winning makes them hungry." The most honest economic indicator in rugby.
news.wWin5: A lad in the family stand has started bringing a homemade cardboard trophy. Three straight wins. His dad keeps apologising to the row behind and nobody minds.
news.wWinOn1: The winning run rolls on and the ground has stopped whispering about it. Away fans arrive expecting the worst now, which is the highest compliment a terrace can pay.
news.wWinOn2: Still winning. The older heads have given up saying "long season" and started asking about final tickets, quietly, in case saying it out loud breaks something.
news.wWinOn3: The run goes on, and the club shop has sold out of scarves in October. Somebody in the sponsors' lounge used the word "era". Nobody laughed.
news.wLose1: Three straight defeats and the phone-ins have turned. One season-ticket holder of 30 years: "I don't see a plan out there." Win this weekend and it all goes quiet - that's football... no, that's rugby.

news.campHeatSubj: ☀️ Camp report: sharp, brown and slightly broken
news.campHeat: A week of double sessions in serious heat. The GPS numbers are the best the staff have ever logged in pre-season, and the group tightened the way only shared suffering manages. £400k well spent, probably.
news.campHomeSubj: 🏟 Community week: the town turns out
news.campHome: Open training drew a four-figure crowd on a Tuesday. Every school in the area got a visit, every junior club got a coach. It cost almost nothing and bought the kind of goodwill money cannot.
news.campTour: Two exhibition matches, three time zones, one very happy sponsor and £600k in the bank. The supporters grumble about a pre-season spent in departure lounges, and the squad starts the year with heavy legs.
news.toneSwaggerSubj: Swagger alert: is all that praise going to their heads?
news.toneSwagger: Your players can't stop telling the press how good they are - because you keep telling the press how good they are. The assistant's note is blunt: "Training tempo has dipped. They think they only need to turn up." Expect flat performances until someone puts a shift in - or until you sharpen your tongue.
news.toneBruisedSubj: Dressing room bruised by public criticism
news.toneBruised: Week after week of hard words in press conferences has landed. Senior players are reportedly "sick of being thrown under the bus" and morale has sagged across the squad. A little public warmth would go a long way.

news.townCollection: The supporters' trust organised a collection for {club}: {amount}, in coins and notes and one farmer's cheque, handed over before training. The town does not intend to lose this club.
news.healSubj: 🏥 The retreat: a clean bill of health
news.heal: The specialist retreat has done its work: {n} of the squad walked out with a clean bill of health. Every injury cleared, every man fresh. Match sharpness is the one thing medicine cannot buy - that comes back on Saturdays.
news.estate: The contractors have gone and the scaffolding with them: every facility at {club} now stands at its ceiling. Nine world-class buildings - and world-class running costs, which the books will feel every week.
news.pinnacle: Your name has gone to the federations, with a full dossier of your work attached. These things move quickly once they move at all: expect an approach within a fortnight.
news.dressingDownSubj: Dressing room whispers: {player} unhappy after dressing-down
news.dressingDown: Word has leaked that {player} was hauled in front of the coach over his recent form - and didn't take it well. Team-mates say he trained on his own on Tuesday.
news.boardPushedSubj: FORMAL WARNING: the board's answer stands
news.boardPushed: You were given a decision and you came back at the door regardless. The board takes that as a challenge to its authority, and says so in writing: the answer has not changed, confidence in your judgement is severely dented, and the next repetition of this conversation will be your last at the club.
news.sackedPushed: Warned in writing, and back at the boardroom door within the month anyway. The board decided the club needed a manager who could hear a no. {era} Your reputation travels with you - and so does the story of how this ended.
news.dreamRefocus: You set out to {dream_k}, and it is done. A manager needs a reason: when you are ready, name a new dream from the Legacy screen. The one you realised stays on the record for good.
news.sponsorEnded: {short} and {sponsor} have parted ways before the end of the {slot_k} deal, at the club's request. The money stops immediately - and three new parties have already been in touch about the vacant slot. Their terms are their own: some markets reward a club back on the market, some make it pay for the interruption.
news.natAppointed: It is official: you are the head coach of {nat_k}. Test windows, championship campaigns, and every trophy goes in your cabinet; your assistant takes the club whenever your country plays. One thing left - whether you carry on at the club. Answer it on your Manager Profile.
news.natAppointedOnly: It is official. You are the head coach of {nat_k}. Test windows, championship campaigns, and every trophy they win goes in YOUR cabinet - and with no club on the desk, the country has your whole week.
news.fanSoldStar: {player} has gone to {to} and {club}'s support are not taking it well: the forums say this is a club selling its best and buying nobody, and one supporter has changed his profile picture to a black square. Fan mood down {n}.
news.fanSoldIcon: There is a difference between selling a player and selling one of their own, and {club}'s support know which this is. {player} has joined {to}. There is a bedsheet on the fence, and the phone-in ran ninety minutes with nobody defending it. Fan mood down {n}.
news.fanSignedStarSubj: 🎉 {player} signs - and the town has noticed
news.fanSignedStar: {player} is a {club} player. The announcement video has been watched more times than the town has residents, the club shop has sold out of the letters in his name, and a local bakery is doing a limited-edition pastry nobody can describe. Fan mood is up {n}. {rival_k}
news.fanSignedIconSubj: 🚨 THEY'VE ONLY GONE AND SIGNED HIM: {player}
news.fanSignedIcon: There were people on the streets. Actual people, on a Tuesday. {player} has signed for {club} and the town has lost all proportion: two babies named after the manager, a man tattooed somewhere he will regret, the club song eleven times before lunch. Fan mood up {n}. {rival_k}
news.fanRivalNamed: In the dressing room the mood is more complicated: {rival} has just watched his shirt get a great deal harder to keep.
news.fanRivalNone: Nobody in the squad plays where he plays, which is exactly why he was signed.
news.fanRumble: It is not a campaign yet. It is a tone. {boss} is being discussed rather than backed, the forums have a thread that is now nine pages long, and the word "direction" is being used a lot. Results settle this quickly, one way or the other.
news.fanBanners: A section of the {club} support has organised: banners in the away end's eyeline, a hashtag, a petition with more names than the ground holds. The board have been asked about it twice this week and answered carefully both times. It costs {boss} confidence every week it runs.
news.fanPlane: They hired a plane. It flew over {stadium} for eleven minutes trailing a message about {boss}, and that photograph is now the picture every outlet uses for this club. The directors are no longer asked whether they back the manager. They are asked when.
news.fanForgiven: The banners are gone, the thread has died, and the singing on Saturday started before kick-off rather than after the first score. {club}'s support have decided they are behind {boss} after all. It buys time - not for ever, but the kind of time a manager can actually use.
news.upStormSubj: 🌬 The gale took the South Stand tarpaulin
news.upStorm: Three days of wind and {stadium} has lost most of the covering on the South Stand, two advertising boards and, for reasons the groundsman cannot explain, a wheelie bin that was later found in the car park of a garden centre. The repair comes to {amount}. The bin has been returned.
news.upRoof: The five-year survey on {stadium} came back with the word "urgent" in it more times than anybody would like. Steelwork, guttering and a section of cladding that has apparently been held on by paint since the nineties. {amount}, and the surveyor would like it known that he did warn them.
news.upPipeSubj: 💧 A burst pipe under the away changing room
news.upPipe: It went at four in the morning, which is the only good news in the story, and the away changing room at {stadium} spent six hours as a paddling pool. New flooring, new benches, and a plumber who kept saying "well there's your problem" without ever specifying what it was. {amount}.
news.upFloodlightsSubj: 💡 Two floodlight columns fail the inspection
news.upFloodlights: The lighting engineer walked round {stadium} with a clipboard and a look, and two columns did not pass. Replacement heads, a crane for a day, and a Tuesday night fixture that came within an hour of being played in what he cheerfully called "heritage lighting". {amount}.
news.upPitchSubj: 🌱 The pitch has to be relaid
news.upPitch: The drainage has given up, the far corner has been more mud than grass since November, and the groundsman has started referring to it as "the bog" in official documents. A full hybrid relay at {stadium}: {amount}. He says it will be worth it. He is right, and he will not stop saying it.
news.upForkliftSubj: 🚜 A forklift, a hospitality suite, and a very quiet meeting
news.upForklift: Nobody has been named. Everybody knows. A forklift reversed through the partition wall of the hospitality suite at {stadium} on a Thursday afternoon, and the club is now short one partition wall, one drinks fridge and a print of the 1998 squad that the chairman was fond of. {amount}, and a new policy about who may drive what.
news.upBadger: A protected species has taken a serious interest in the drainage at {stadium}, and the law is extremely clear about who has to move. Ecologist, licence, exclusion fencing and a specialist relocation: {amount}. The groundsman has stopped speaking to anyone about it.
news.upDinnerSubj: 🥂 The sportsman's dinner went off like a rocket
news.upDinner: Sold out in nine hours, a comedian who was funnier than he was expensive, and an auction that got completely out of hand when two local builders started bidding against each other for a signed shirt neither of them wanted. {club} are {amount} better off and the builders are no longer speaking.
news.upBeerFestSubj: 🍺 The beer festival was rained on for three days
news.upBeerFest: Two hundred barrels, a marquee, a folk duo, and the wettest weekend since records began at {stadium}. The marquee held. The car park did not. What was budgeted as the summer's big earner is a loss of {amount}, and there is a great deal of beer in the cellar that somebody will have to drink.
news.upWeddingSubj: 💍 The function room is booked out until June
news.upWedding: Somebody in the commercial department had the idea of marketing {stadium} for weddings, and it has worked far better than anyone expected. Every Saturday is spoken for, the club has bought a second dance floor, and the groundsman has been asked twice whether the pitch can be walked on in heels. {amount} to the good.
news.upConcertSubj: 🎤 A stadium concert, and the grass will forgive us
news.upConcert: Forty thousand people, one very famous act, and a stage build that took eleven days. {stadium} banks {amount}, the groundsman has aged visibly, and the far touchline will be a slightly different colour until March. The board have already asked when the next one is.
news.upFunRunSubj: 🏃 The fun run raised more than expected
news.upFunRun: Fourteen hundred people ran round {stadium} in fancy dress on a Sunday morning. A man in a full front-row scrum costume, alone, finished in under an hour and became briefly famous. After costs the club is {amount} up, and the local paper got a photograph it will use for years.
news.upSantaGrottoSubj: 🎅 The grotto did not go to plan
news.upSantaGrotto: The idea was a Christmas grotto in the East Stand concourse. The execution involved a queue that stretched into the car park, a reindeer that was clearly a pony, and a Santa who had to be replaced at short notice for reasons the club will not be commenting on. Down {amount}, and the pony has been asked back.
news.upFilmCrewSubj: 🎬 A film crew have taken over the ground
news.upFilmCrew: Something with a big budget and a lot of drizzle in it is being shot at {stadium} for a fortnight. The club is {amount} up, catering has never been better, and three academy lads have been paid to stand in the background looking disappointed, which they described afterwards as the easiest money of their lives.
news.upClubhouseSubj: 🍻 The clubhouse has become the place to be
news.upClubhouse: Somebody put a proper coffee machine in, somebody else started a Thursday quiz, and the clubhouse at {stadium} has quietly turned into the busiest room in the town. Takings are up, the committee are delighted, and a local darts team has asked whether they can move in permanently. {amount} to the good.

press.banQ1: The citing commissioner has upheld {player}'s red card: a {n}-match ban. The club has 48 hours to appeal. Do you?

banQ2.one: {player}'s suspension is confirmed this morning - {n} match. Half your inbox is lawyers who fancy the footage. Appeal it?
banQ2.other: {player}'s suspension is confirmed this morning - {n} matches. Half your inbox is lawyers who fancy the footage. Appeal it?

banQ3.one: The panel was not moved: {n} match for {player}. The supporters call it a stitch-up. Fight it, or take it?
banQ3.other: The panel was not moved: {n} matches for {player}. The supporters call it a stitch-up. Fight it, or take it?

press.banAppealR: The paperwork goes in overnight and the hearing is fast-tracked. The verdict lands in your inbox the same day.
press.banAcceptR: No circus, no lawyers. The panel notes the club's professionalism, and the player serves his time quietly.
press.banBlastR: The dressing room loves it. The league office adds a note to your file, and the next fifty-fifty call may remember this.
press.finalQ1: Finals week. The room is three deep, half of them faces you have never seen. {comp}, {where}, {opp} on the other side. The first question is the only one they all came for: can you win it?
press.finalQ2: The camera count has tripled and there is a national broadcaster's anchor in the front row. One game, at {where}, against {opp}, for the {comp}. How do you handle a week like this?
press.finalQ3: Every seat taken, standing at the back - finals week does this. {opp} at {where} for the {comp}. They want a headline. What do you give them?
press.finalWin: 'We are ready. We will win it'
press.finalWinR: The back pages have their headline and the dressing room walks taller all week. If Saturday goes wrong, that sentence will be read back to you for years.
press.finalRespectR: Measured and confident. The board approves, the players nod along, and nobody has been handed a team-talk quote.
press.finalTrap: 'The occasion is the trap - it is just rugby'
press.finalTrapR: You talk the week down to protect the group. Sensible - though one or two of the younger lads wanted to hear the fire.
press.hotQ1: {player} has been in scintillating form - some are calling him the best {pos_k} in the competition. Do you agree?
press.hotQ2: The whole league is purring about {player}. Best {pos_k} in the competition right now: yes or no?
press.hotQ3: {player} again at the weekend. The pundits have run out of superlatives - have you?
press.hotPraiseR: {player} is reportedly delighted with your public backing.
press.hotFeet: Keep his feet on the ground
press.hotFeetR: A measured response. {player} knows there is more to do.
press.hotOthersR: You spread the praise across the whole side. {player} nods along, and the pack notes the mention of the men who win him his ball.
press.noCommentR: The press pack grumbles and moves on.
press.coldQ1: {player} has looked well short of his best in recent weeks. Is his place under threat?
press.coldQ2: Be honest about {player} - the supporters on the message boards already are. What is going wrong for him?
press.coldQ3: {player} would struggle to make most sides in this league on current form. Does he keep the shirt?
press.coldBackR: {player} appreciates the show of faith and vows to repay it.
press.coldAdmitR: Honest, but {player} is stung by the criticism.
press.coldBlameR: "If he is short of form, look at how I am using him." The room did not expect that. {player} did not either - and he trains like a man with a debt to repay.
press.coldNoOneR: You deflect the question with a straight bat.
press.rumourQ1: We're hearing strong links between {player} and {club}. What's your message to worried supporters?
press.rumourQ2: {club} scouts were in the stand again, and everyone knows who they came to watch. Is {player} for sale?
press.rumourQ3: {player} to {club} is the story that will not die. Kill it now, if you can.
press.rumourNeverR: A firm line. {player} feels wanted; {short} are said to be undeterred.
press.rumourPriceR: {player}'s agent has taken note. Expect the phone to ring.
press.rumourAskR: You hand the question to the player, publicly and warmly. {player} obliges with a straight answer about loving the club, which buries the story better than any denial of yours could.
press.derbyQ1: {derby} this weekend. {opp_k} say the pressure is all on you. Your response?
press.derbyQ2: It is {derby} week and the town talks of nothing else. {opp_k} reckon the pressure sits with you. Does it?
press.derbyQ3: {poss_k} players have been talking in the papers all week ahead of {derby}. Rise to it, or rise above it?
press.derbyFanR: The back pages love it. The town is at boiling point - your players will feel ten feet tall, or feel the heat.
press.derbyJustR: Nobody believes you, least of all your own supporters.
press.derbyPraiseR: A statesmanlike answer. Both sets of fans nod approvingly, then go back to hating each other.
press.kidQ1: Everyone is talking about {player} - {age} years old and lighting up the league. Is he the future of the club?
press.kidQ2: {player}, {age}, and already the first name the supporters sing. How good can he actually be?
press.kidQ3: Scouts, agents, pundits: all of them asking about {player}. Is the club ready for what comes next?
press.kidCrownR: {player} floats out of the press room - and every scout in the hemisphere just circled his name.
press.kidProtectR: Measured. He keeps developing away from the circus.
press.kidEarn: He plays when he earns it
press.kidEarnR: Old school. {player} bristles, but the senior players approve.
press.raceQ1: The title race is down to you and {club}. {coach_k} says his side "handles the big moments better". Care to respond?
press.raceQ2: {coach_k} lit the fuse this morning: his {short} side "handles the big moments better", apparently. Your reply?
press.raceQ3: Two horses left in this race, and the other one is {club}. They are talking a big game across town. Anything to send back?
press.racePressureR: "{short} have everything to lose - we're loving this." The squad walks taller; the run-in just got personal.
press.raceOurselvesR: Calm, professional, forgettable. The dressing room stays level.
press.raceFlatterR: You call {short} "the best side in the league". Pundits call it mind games. Maybe it is.
press.unveilQ1: {player} is in the room for his unveiling, shirt in hand. What are you expecting from your new {pos_k}?
press.unveilQ2: New shirt, new number, cameras everywhere: {player} is officially yours. What did you sign him to do?
press.unveilQ3: {player} has just finished posing for the photographers. Tell the supporters what their new {pos_k} brings.
press.unveilMarqueeR: "He changes everything for us." {player} beams - and every match report this season will measure him against that sentence.
press.unveilSettleR: Sensible. The pressure valve stays closed while he learns the calls.
press.unveilFightR: A cold shower at his own unveiling. The squad notes that nobody gets given a shirt here.
press.crisisQ1: {n} defeats in the last {of}. Supporters are restless. How do you respond to talk of a crisis?
press.crisisQ2: {n} losses from {of}. The word "crisis" was said on the radio this morning. Is it one?
press.crisisQ3: The table does not lie: beaten {n} times in your last {of}. What do you say to supporters who have stopped believing?
press.crisisOwnR: The dressing room respects your honesty.
press.crisisMarginsR: The board is unimpressed with excuses.
press.crisisAttackR: The clip goes viral for the wrong reasons.
press.cardsQ1: {n} cards at the weekend, {man_k} among them. Is there a discipline problem in your squad?
press.cardsQ2: {Man_k} in the book again - {n} cards in one afternoon. When does passion become a problem?
press.cardsQ3: The disciplinary summary makes grim reading: {n} cards. Whose fault is that - the players' or the coaching?
press.cardsDefendR: The squad appreciates the shield. The disciplinary panel does not.
press.cardsAddressR: Sternly said. Extra tackling-technique sessions are already booked.
press.cardsBlameR: The players love it; the league office sends a warning letter.
press.ownerQ1: The takeover is done and the new owner is in the building. Every manager in your position is one bad month from a "restructure". What is your message to him?
press.ownerQ2: New owner, first week. History says managers rarely survive a regime change. Why will you be different?
press.ownerQ3: The new owner watched training from the balcony this morning, arms folded. What does he need to hear from you?
press.ownerRugbyR: Confident, direct - owners like a man who volunteers for the scoreboard.
press.ownerVision: We are aligned on the vision
press.ownerVisionR: Fluent boardroom-speak. The suits nod; the terraces roll their eyes.
press.ownerComeGoR: The dressing room loves the defiance. Upstairs, a note is made.
press.vultureQ1: There are reports this morning that the board has sounded out potential replacements. Are you fighting for your job?
press.vultureQ2: Names are circulating for your job - real names, with real agents. Do you still have the board's backing?
press.vultureQ3: A bookmaker suspended betting on the next manager here this morning. How safe are you, honestly?
press.vultureTrophiesR: Defiant. The players walk a little taller - now you have to deliver.
press.vultureBoard: That is a question for the board
press.vultureBoardR: The vacuum fills with more speculation.
press.vultureLaughR: The room chuckles. The chairman, watching the stream, does not.
press.runInSecond: Second, and breathing down their necks
press.runInQ1: Top {where_k} with the season on the line. Can this group handle the pressure of a run-in?
press.runInQ2: {pile_k} with the business end here. Do your players sleep at night?
press.runInQ3: Every week from now is a final. {who_k} always claim to enjoy it - do you, actually?
press.runInTarget: We want the target on our backs
press.runInTargetR: Bold. The bookies shorten your odds; the players feed off it.
press.runInOneGameR: The oldest line in the book, delivered with a straight face.
press.runInPrivilegeR: Instant back-page headline. The town believes.
press.intlQ1: {n} of your players are away on international duty. Should clubs be compensated when the Test windows strip their squads?
press.intlQ2: {n} first-teamers gone to the Test window and half your dressing room is empty. Proud, or fed up?
press.intlQ3: The internationals have taken {n} of yours this window. Is the club-versus-country tug of war broken?
press.intlProudR: Gracious - and the academy parents noticed.
press.intlCalendarR: Half the league's coaches text you in agreement.
press.intlCopeR: Brisk. The fringe players hear the message: their chance is coming.
press.intlFringe: The fringe get their shot now
press.intlFringeR: Ten men who train all week and watch all weekend just sat up straighter.
press.intlMoneyR: The chairman applauds from upstairs. The unions send a lawyer's letter.
press.intlFamiliesR: A warm line that costs nothing and travels. Two mums frame the clipping.
press.intlDepth: Judge my squad depth in May
press.intlDepthR: Confident. The pundits write it down for later, which is how promises work.
press.intlClub: I pick clubs over country, always
press.intlClubR: The terraces love it. Three national coaches stop returning your calls.
press.intlHurtsR: Candid, and the room respects it - but the headline writes itself: COACH ADMITS CRISIS.
press.natQ1: Your {nation_k} squad is in camp and the country is watching. What does this window need to deliver?
press.natQ2: Two jobs, one weekend: the nation's press want to know where {nationThe_k} sits on your list. Well?
press.natQ3: The {nation_k} squad you named has the phone-ins arguing already. Talk us through your thinking.
press.natWinLotR: The union loves it - and has written it down. Deliver, or this window becomes the stick they beat you with.
press.natTestByTestR: Measured. The federation nods; the phone-ins move on to the referees.
press.natClubPaysR: Your dressing room walks taller. In the federation offices, someone underlines a clause.
press.unbeatenQ1: {n} league games, {n} wins. Nobody has laid a glove on you. Go on - say the word.
press.unbeatenQ2: Still unbeaten in the league. What is the secret, and when does the weight of the run start to tell?
press.unbeatenQ3: An unbeaten season is quietly becoming a real conversation. Is it on?
press.unbeatenNothingR: Straight bat. The senior players nod along.
press.unbeatenSayItR: The town roars. The board swallows hard - that quote will follow you into every ground.
press.unbeatenStandard: The run will end. The standard will not
press.unbeatenStandardR: Composed and quotable. Both rooms are happy.
press.plansQ1: {player} knocks and closes the door behind him. "Boss, I have barely played all season. Tell me straight - am I in your plans or not?"
press.plansQ2: {player} has been waiting outside since the end of training. "I watch every session from the sidelines, boss. I need to know if there is a future for me here."
press.plansQ3: {player} does not sit down. "I am not here to argue. One question: do you see me in this team? Because right now I cannot."
press.plansIn: You are in my plans - stay ready
press.plansInR1: {player} leaves with his head up. He will hold you to it - pick him soon or this conversation happens again, louder.
press.plansInR2: The tension goes out of his shoulders. A promise in this office is a promise on the team sheet - he will be counting the weeks.
press.plansOut: Honestly? He can find a new club
press.plansOutR1: A hard truth, kindly delivered. {player} thanks you for being straight - and his agent is making calls within the hour.
press.plansOutR2: He goes quiet, then nods. "Appreciate the honesty, boss." The listing will not shock anyone in the dressing room.
press.plansEarn: Nobody is owed a shirt here
press.plansEarnR1: He nods, jaw tight, and heads back to training. The squad hears about it - the honest ones respect it.
press.plansEarnR2: "Fine. Then I will take one." He trains like a man possessed all week. That answer either made him or lost him.
press.loanQ1: {player}, {age}, is waiting by your office after training. "I am not learning anything carrying tackle bags, boss. Send me on loan - I need real minutes."
press.loanQ2: {player} catches you in the corridor, all nerves and rehearsed lines. "Boss, my mates from the age-groups are playing senior rugby every week. I am standing still here. Let me go and prove it somewhere."
press.loanQ3: The academy coach sends {player} up to see you. The lad gets it out in one breath: "Loan me out, boss. I will come back better - or I will come back and you can tell me I was wrong."
press.loanMinutesR1: {player} lights up. Play him in the next few weeks or the shine wears off fast.
press.loanMinutesR2: He floats out of the office. A first-team promise at his age is rocket fuel - but it burns fast if the team sheet never shows it.
press.loanAgreeR1: A smart development call. The loan is agreed the same afternoon, and the reports will come back to you every few weeks.
press.loanAgreeR2: He grins and shakes your hand twice, and the academy coach makes the calls before you have changed your mind: minutes make players, benches make excuses.
press.loanStay: He is not ready to leave
press.loanStayR1: He trudges out without a word. The academy coach thinks you have just cooled your hottest prospect.
press.loanStayR2: "Right." One word, and the door does not slam, which is somehow worse. Keep an eye on his training reports.
press.dealQ1: {player}, {age} now, sits down across from you. "My deal is up this summer. I am not asking for promises, boss - I just need to know if I should be planning a life after this place."
press.dealQ2: {player} waits until the room is empty. "Twelve years a professional, boss, and this is the conversation you never get used to. My contract is up. Where do I stand?"
press.dealQ3: {player} brings two coffees in and sets one down in front of you. "No agents, no lawyers, just us. My deal ends this summer. Tell me what you are thinking."
press.dealYear: There is another year in you
press.dealYearR1: {player} shakes your hand hard. Offer the terms from his player page before someone else does.
press.dealYearR2: Relief, then a grin you have not seen since pre-season. Get the paperwork moving before his agent hears anything else.
press.dealLast: This season is his last here
press.dealLastR1: He takes it with dignity. He will finish the job properly - and the young players just saw how endings are handled here.
press.dealLastR2: A long exhale, a nod, a handshake. "Then let us win something on the way out." Class to the end.
press.dealWaitR1: Honest, but the uncertainty follows him around. His agent quietly starts taking other calls.
press.dealWaitR2: He expected better than a maybe. The performances will tell you his answer before you give him yours.
press.routQ1: {us}-{them}. A statement performance - the best this team can play, or is there more?
press.routQ2: {us}-{them}, and it barely flattered you. Where does that rank among performances in your time here?
press.routQ3: {opp} had no answers out there. {us}-{them} - is this side at its ceiling, or still climbing?
press.routMoreR: Ominous for the rest of the league. The players believe it too.
press.routMoveOnR: All business. The standard is the standard.
press.thrashQ1: {us}-{them} to {opp}. Supporters deserve an explanation. What went wrong out there?
press.thrashQ2: {us}-{them}. Some of your supporters left twenty minutes early. What do you owe them?
press.thrashQ3: A {by}-point beating. Talk us through it, because nobody in the stands could.
press.thrashOnMe: That was on me, not the players
press.thrashOnMeR: The dressing room notices who took the bullets.
press.thrashUnacceptableR: Hard words, publicly delivered. Training will be spiky this week.
press.thrashOneDayR: Calm - but the phone-ins want blood, not calm.
press.derbyWonQ1: Derby day belongs to you. The fans are singing your name outside - a message for them?
press.derbyWonQ2: You could hear your end from the tunnel. A derby won: who does it mean more to, you or them?
press.derbyWonQ3: Bragging rights are yours until the return fixture. Any words for the neighbours?
press.derbyWonEnjoyR: The clip of your grin does big numbers. Bragging rights secured.
press.derbyWonFour: It is only worth four points
press.derbyWonFourR: True, technically. Nobody outside the building agrees.
press.derbyWonCityR: Front page. Their fans will keep the receipt - mind the return fixture.
press.derbyLostQ1: A derby defeat, and their supporters are letting you know about it. How do you face your own fans this week?
press.derbyLostQ2: They will paint the town their colours tonight. A derby lost - how long does this one hurt?
press.derbyLostQ3: Your supporters filed out in silence; theirs did not. What happens now?
press.derbyLostFace: We will not hide from this
press.derbyLostFaceR: Straight talk. The fans respect honesty more than excuses.
press.derbyLostStatsR: The stats might back you up. Derby crowds do not deal in stats.
press.derbyLostReturnR: A promise. It will be remembered - deliver or else.
press.discTraining: The assistant closes the door: {player} skipped Monday's recovery session and did not think it worth an excuse. The squad knows, and the squad is watching what you do about it.
press.discForm: The assistant closes the door: {player} has been well below his own standard, and the coaches say the effort in review meetings matches the ratings. The squad knows, and the squad is watching what you do about it.
press.discWord: A quiet word, man to man
press.slotQ: The {slot_k} is on a stopgap arrangement at {weekly} a week - under the going rate. The commercial director has three offers on the desk. Which way do we go?

slotLongR.one: Signed. Safe money for {n} year - a touch under market, because the sponsor is buying certainty off you.
slotLongR.other: Signed. Safe money for {n} years - a touch under market, because the sponsor is buying certainty off you.

slotShortR.one: Signed. Over the market rate, and you are back at this desk in {n} year - which is the bet: your reputation will have grown by then.
slotShortR.other: Signed. Over the market rate, and you are back at this desk in {n} years - which is the bet: your reputation will have grown by then.

press.slotClauseR: Signed, with the clause. Deliver on the pitch and it is the best deal in the building; fall short and you sold cheap.
press.slotKeep: Stay with the stopgap for now
press.slotKeepR: The stopgap rolls on at a discount. The offers stay on the Finances screen whenever you want them.
press.refereeQ1: Two penalties in the last ten minutes, both against you, both at the breakdown. Anything you'd like to say about the officiating?
press.refereeQ2: {n} late penalties, all one way, and a game lost by a score. Was that refereed fairly?
press.refereeClips: I'll be sending the clips to the union.
press.refereeClipsR: Fined by the disciplinary panel by Wednesday. Your pack loved it. The terraces loved it more.
press.refereeOurs: Referees make decisions. We made more mistakes than he did.
press.refereeOursR: The pundits call it grown-up. The pack calls it something else, quietly, on the bus.
press.refereeUnseenR: Everyone in the room knows you have. The line dies on the table and nobody picks it up.
press.standoffQ1: {player} is out of contract in the summer and hasn't signed. Has he told you he's leaving?
press.standoffQ2: Still nothing on {player}'s new deal. Is he waiting for a better offer, or are you?
press.standoffLoved: He'll sign. He knows where he's loved.
press.standoffLovedR: Confident. {player} reads it and smiles. If he doesn't sign, this is the clip they'll run.
press.standoffBigger: Nobody is bigger than the club.
press.standoffBiggerR: Firm. His agent posts a single eyes emoji. Three clubs like it.
press.standoffBetween: That's between the player and the club.
press.standoffBetweenR: The room writes 'stand-off' in inverted commas, which is worse than writing it without them.
press.weatherQ1: Forty millimetres forecast for Saturday at {opp}. You're a running side. Do you change how you play?
press.weatherQ2: It's January, it's {opp} away and the pitch is a bog. Where does the rugby go?
press.weatherKick: We'll kick it, and we'll kick it well.
press.weatherKickR: Your fly-half nods slowly. Your wingers stop listening around the word 'kick'.
press.weatherSame: We play the same rugby in any weather.
press.weatherSameR: Brave. Damp. The board admires the principle from a heated box.
press.weatherCoatR: Gets a laugh. Gets printed. Gets a coat sent to the club by a local outfitter, unasked.
press.oldboyQ1: {player} faces {opp} on Saturday, his old club. Will he be starting, and will he be celebrating?
press.oldboyQ2: First time back for {player} against {opp}. How do you handle a man playing his old mates?
press.oldboyCelebrate: He'll start, and he can celebrate how he likes.
press.oldboyCelebrateR: He scores. He celebrates. Their end remembers it, and so does yours.
press.oldboyBehaveR: He behaves. He also has his quietest game of the season, which may be related.
press.oldboyFridayR: You have never once announced a team on a Friday, and the room knows it.
press.kidstartQ1: {player} is nineteen and starting at {pos_k} against a side that will know it. Brave or reckless?
press.kidstartQ2: A first start for {player} at nineteen. What does he know at kick-off that he didn't know this morning?
press.kidstartReadyR: He's ready. His mother is not. {senior} watches from the bench with an expression.
press.kidstartInjuries: We've got injuries. He's what we have.
press.kidstartInjuriesR: Honest. He reads it. He plays like a man who has read it.
press.kidstartFirstR: Warm, and true, and he plays like it - like a man having a first game.
press.seatsQ1: {n} empty seats on Saturday. Are the supporters telling you something?
press.seatsQ2: Three home games, three half-empty stands. Whose fault is that?
press.seatsListeningR: The supporters' trust invites you to their AGM. You go. Upstairs would rather you hadn't admitted anything.
press.seatsPricesR: The commercial director's department reads that before you've left the room.
press.seatsWinR: They do, eventually. Nobody has ever said 'eventually' in a press conference and enjoyed it.
press.leakQ1: We're hearing {player} has been dropped for Saturday - before you've told him. Who's talking in your dressing room?
press.leakQ2: {player}'s name was on a team sheet in a pub last night, and not the one you've handed in. Where's the leak?
press.leakLong: Somebody who won't be in it for long.
press.leakLongR: Menacing. Nobody confesses. Three people stop talking to each other, and one of them is innocent.
press.leakStarts: You've got it wrong. He starts.
press.leakStartsR: You now have to start {player}. He knows it. So does the man he replaces.
press.leakTalkR: A shrug. The leaker leaks again by Thursday, encouraged.
press.centuryQ1: {player}'s {what_k} on Saturday. Is he the best you've worked with?
press.centuryQ2: A {what_k} for {player}. What does he mean to this place?
press.centuryBestR: He's told. Twice. By his mates. {captain_k}
press.centuryCaptainSulks: {captain} hears it too, and says nothing, pointedly.
press.centuryConversationR: Diplomatic. He noticed the word 'conversation' and will mention it at Christmas.
press.centuryTwoHundred: Ask me after he's got to two hundred.
press.centuryTwoHundredR: A laugh, and a target. He has a hundred to go and has already started counting.
press.benchQ1: {player} hasn't started in six weeks. His agent says he's 'exploring options'. Are you?
press.benchQ2: Six weeks on the bench for {player}, and he's better than that. What's he done?
press.benchDoor: He can explore. My door's open.
press.benchDoorR: It is. He walks through it on Monday with a transfer request and a printout.
press.benchBuilding: He's a big part of what we're building.
press.benchBuildingR: He has read that sentence before, in two other programmes, about two other men.
press.benchNextWeekR: {player} starts next week. You have just picked your team in a press conference.
press.comebackQ1: Down by {n} at the break. What on earth did you say at half time?
press.comebackQ2: Fifteen behind and out. Then not. Talk us through the dressing room at half time.
press.comebackCaptain: Nothing. I let the captain speak.
press.comebackCaptainR: {captain} becomes a folk hero by teatime. You become 'the quiet one', which you can live with.
press.comebackTruthR: Which was, according to a source in the room, quite loud and mostly accurate.
press.comebackRoomR: Everyone respects it. Everyone tries to find out. Somebody will, by Wednesday.

till.boardBlurb: The Charter is real money through the app store, signed into this save with no way back - and never needed to win.
till.injWage: The board underwrites {weekly} of wages outside the cap until summer.
till.injNone: The owners will not go to the well again this year.
till.xlWait: The Sugar Daddy calls once a day. Ready again in about {h}h.
till.injLanded: The funds have landed: {amount} added to the budget and the books.
till.injHeld: Paid, and held: the board will not vote it through again this season. It stays yours - this page will offer it again when the well refills.
till.pending: The store is still processing it. Nothing more to do - when it lands, this page will offer it to the career in front of you.
till.charterBody: New ownership arrives with lawyers and the league's salary cap stops applying to this club. No ceiling, no fines, no embargoes - permanent, for this save alone, and the save wears the 🖋 mark for good. Every other club stays capped.
till.charterConfirm: Remove it - there is no way back
till.charterDone: 🖋 Done. The wage law no longer applies to this club.
till.charterSigned: The cap is gone and the save wears the mark: no ceiling, no fines, no embargoes, for as long as this career runs.
till.charterOwned: You own this. Turn it on below when you are certain - it cannot be turned off.
till.fineprint: Prices are the store's own. A consumable purchase is only ever spent once it has visibly landed in your career; if anything is interrupted, this page offers the purchase back. Nothing here plays the matches.

store.title: Store
store.bought: Yours. It follows your store account - Restore brings it back on a new phone.
store.needCareer: Open a career first - the retreat needs a squad to visit.
store.removeAdsLine: Every ad in the game, gone for good.
store.healLine: Every injury healed, the whole squad fresh. Once per match played.
store.healDone: Done: the whole squad reports fit.
store.healNobody: Paid, and held: there is nobody to mend right now. It stays yours - apply it when it counts.
store.creditGone: Nothing left to apply here. If the store refunded an older purchase, it can simply be bought again.
store.healWait: The retreat needs a match between visits - play one and it reopens.
store.pinnacleLine: Pick a federation and you are their head coach on the spot.
store.callMade: Appointed: you are the head coach of {nat}. Your Manager Profile asks the one thing left - do you carry on at the club?
store.callRefused: Not now: you already hold a national job, a federation matter is open, or this career has had its call.
store.estateLine: Every facility to its maximum, for the club that builds it.
store.estateConfirm: Build it - the whole estate, for good
store.estateDone: 🏗️ Done. Nine world-class facilities, and the running costs to match.
store.estateRefused: Nothing to build: the estate is already at its ceiling.
store.charterLine: No wage ceiling, ever again, on the save that turns it on.
store.fundingLine: Four board resolutions, £10m to £130m, each with a season of cap-exempt wages.
store.fineprint: One-off payments, handled by the app store. Nothing here plays the matches, and the game still sends nothing about you anywhere.
store.tillSilent: The store is connected but has not answered yet. Buying can still work - its own sheet opens before anything is charged. If this build just arrived, give it a minute.
store.tillPartial: The store answered for {live} of {asked} products. The others may not be on sale to this account yet.
store.pickNation: Yours. Pick the federation and take the job - the appointment is immediate.
store.supportLine: A thank-you to the developer. It changes nothing in the game.

settings.title: Settings
settings.sub: How the game looks, not how it plays
settings.skinLine: Every screen, repainted. Nothing about the rugby changes.
settings.skinDefaultLine: The green and gold the game was built in.
settings.skinMidnightLine: Navy and electric cyan. The gantry view, all telestrator and no tea urn.
settings.skinHeritageLine: Oatmeal and deep burgundy. Reads like a Sunday broadsheet that still calls it rugby football.
settings.skinStealthLine: True black and one clean accent. Nothing on screen but the numbers.
settings.floodOn: They are on - the dark ground, which is how most people play.
settings.floodOff: They are off - daylight, for reading in the sun.
settings.langLine: The whole game, not just the menus.
settings.textSizeLine: Bigger type, same game - every screen still fits the phone.
settings.fineprint: These live on this phone, not in the save - a career carried to another device arrives in that one’s colours. Currently reading in {lang}.

sack.head: You are out at {club}
sack.ask: The cameras are already outside. You have to say something.
sack.ownedLine: I deserved it. You do not lose that many and get to blame the fixture list. The players gave me everything, the results were mine, and the club is right to want better.
sack.ownedReply: It leads every bulletin by six o’clock. Nobody has a follow-up question, which is its own kind of verdict - and one old pro on the panel says he would have you at his club tomorrow.
sack.spiteLine: Honestly? I did not like the team anyway. Bad squad, worse canteen, and a training pitch a farmer would apologise for. Somebody will win something there in about nine years.
sack.spiteReply: It is a clip before you reach the car park. The supporters’ forum has forty pages on it by tea time and somebody has already made the canteen line into a flag.
sack.unfairLine: It was unfair, and everyone in this room knows it. Injuries all winter, no money in January, and eleven weeks to fix what took ten years to break. Judge me on a full season or do not judge me at all.
sack.unfairReply: Half the room writes “dignified”, the other half writes “excuses”. Both pieces run. That is the press for you - you were never going to get one headline out of this.

difficulty.hardDesc: Less money in the bank, a board that expects more, a physio room that is busier.
difficulty.legendDesc: Half the money, a board with no patience, and injuries that come in pairs.
